correctness.rationale: The orthogonal spectral projections give ||Re(e^{-iθ}T)||²=M² max(cos²θ,r² cos²(θ−β)); this remains true in arbitrary Hilbert dimension and with a zero complement. The difference is A+R cos(2θ−γ), with A=(1−r²)/2>0 and R²−A²=r² sin²β; integrate its absolute value to derive 1/2+[r sinβ−A atan(r sinβ/A)]/pi. Its derivative wrt s=sinβ is r³s²/[pi(A²+r²s²)]>0. Writing x=r sinβ/A, the ratio (x−atan x)/x³ = integral_0^1 v²/(1+x²v²)dv strictly decreases, giving sharp upper/lower cubic coefficients, equality only at stated endpoints/limits. Taylor gives cubic β turn-on; r=1−ε,β=εt gives the uniform compact crossover. Independent numerical quadrature of four generic parameter pairs matched the analytic formula; source checker tests further finite points. Prior published orthogonal-phase endpoint is not claimed new.
